source.extractionNote: 405 variants = 9 Flavour x 3 Size x 3 Shape x 5 State/Disabled combinations. The axes are orthogonal: Size and Shape carry all geometry, Flavour and State/Disabled carry all colour. Structure was extracted over the 9 Size x Shape variants at Flavour=primary/State=default/Disabled=false; colour over all 45 Flavour x State/Disabled variants at Size=small/Shape=rounded. Every one of the 405 variants is covered by the cross-product of the two tables. Re-extracted 2026-10-18 the same way (geometry over Size x Shape at primary/default; colour over all 45 Flavour x State/Disabled at small/rounded), plus a full scan of all 405 variants for token use, untokenised values and axis independence. Button's icons are hidden by default and a hidden instance exposes no layers, so their fill was read from the instance overrides only (read-only); see issues.

summary: Triggers an action from a text label, with optional icons on either side. Nine flavours set how much weight the action carries, three sizes and three shapes fit it to the surface it sits on. The label is the only content a consumer writes, everything else is a variant choice. When an action has no text label, reach for Icon Button rather than hiding this one's label.

intent.primary: The single most important action in a view, one per group. If two buttons both read as primary, the view has two competing goals and that is a layout problem rather than a property one.
intent.positive: Confirms a constructive outcome such as approving or publishing. Reserve it for the confirmation itself, not for every agreeable action, or it stops signalling anything.
intent.negative: Destructive actions the user cannot undo, such as delete or revoke. If the cancel beside it is styled any stronger than subtle, the safe choice becomes the harder one to find.
intent.subtle: A neutral action meant to sit quietly beside a stronger one, typically the cancel next to a primary. It leans on that neighbour for contrast, so on its own it may not read as interactive.
intent.text: A tertiary action inside dense content. It has nothing behind it at rest, so on a coloured or busy surface it stops looking like a control.
intent.outline-subtle: A secondary action on a busy surface where an accent border would compete. It reads as neutral, so it is the wrong choice for the main action on that surface.
intent.outline: A secondary action that still needs to look clickable on its own. Two of them side by side read as equal weight, which is rarely what was intended.
intent.gradient: One promotional or high-emphasis moment, such as an upgrade prompt. It outranks primary, so a screen carrying two of them has no hierarchy left.
intent.text-gradient: The promotional treatment without the filled weight, for a high-emphasis action inside content. The gradient runs across the label itself, so a very short label barely shows it.

size.orderedBy: rootWidth (small 76 < medium 90 < large 98); Figma stores the options in creation order

intent.small: The default, for toolbars, table rows and dense forms where controls sit close together.
intent.medium: For standard forms and dialogs where the button is a deliberate step rather than a dense control.
intent.large: For a call to action that should be easy to hit without precision, typically the confirm on a touch surface.

intent.sharp: Match the container. Correct when the surrounding surface and inputs are square.
intent.rounded: Match the container. The general-purpose choice alongside the system's other rounded controls.
intent.full: A deliberately soft treatment for standalone or promotional actions. Beside rounded controls in the same group it looks unintentional.

state.note: Documentation-only in Figma. In code these are interaction states the implementation drives, not a prop a consumer sets.

intent.default: The resting state, and the only one to use when laying out a static screen.
intent.hover: Documents the pointer-over treatment. The implementation drives this, so choosing it in a layout freezes the button in a state it should not be in.
intent.pressed: Documents the pointer-down treatment, with the same caveat as hover.
intent.focus: Documents the keyboard focus treatment. The one state whose treatment is identical on every flavour.

disabled.note: Modelled as a VARIANT axis in Figma, but boolean in nature; implement as a boolean prop. Only the combination State=default + Disabled=true exists (405 = 9 x 3 x 3 x 5), so there is no hover/pressed/focus treatment for a disabled button by design.

intent.true: The action is unavailable. Say why somewhere nearby, because a disabled control with no explanation is indistinguishable from a broken one.

intent.text: The action the user is about to perform, written as a verb. The button hugs whatever it is given, so a long label widens the control and can break a toolbar row.

intent.true: Adds an icon before the label to reinforce the action at a glance. Choose the glyph deliberately, the slot arrives holding a default that suits almost nothing.
Turning both icons on at small leaves very little room for the label itself. Use a trailing icon for directional or disclosure actions.

internalVariations.options: any glyph in the icon library
internalVariations.intent: Any glyph from the icon library. Both slots arrive holding Verified, which suits almost no real action, so set it deliberately whenever a slot is turned on.
internalVariations.decision: Button does not re-declare this as its own property. Whether it becomes a prop (e.g. leadingIcon: <glyph>) in code is the implementer's call.

internalVariations.property: Size, Framed (VARIANT on the nested Icon)
internalVariations.intent: Button does not re-declare Icon's other properties, but the instance stays exposed, so Icon's glyph, Size and Framed are still reachable in the properties panel. See the Icon Metadata frame for what Icon itself offers, and leave its Size alone, Button pairs it to the label.
internalVariations.decision: Button pins Size per its own Size (small -> Icon small, medium/large -> Icon medium) and Framed=false. Do not expose these.

anatomy.role: The button's own horizontal auto-layout frame. Carries the background, the border and the radius, and holds the height fixed for the chosen Size.
An Icon instance before the label, hidden until Leading Icon is turned on. Button sets its size and leaves the instance exposed.

fill.token: per flavour, following the label (overridden on the instance)
fill.boundInside: Icon binds foreground/primary; Button overrides it in every flavour and in disabled since 2026-10-18

anatomy._boxNote: measured at size=small; the authored value is the nested Icon's Size variant, not a token on Button

anatomy.role: A wrapper frame around the text. Its own horizontal padding is what separates the text from the icons, the row itself has no gap.

padding._note: left/right are token-bound; top/bottom are simply unset (0), not a token

anatomy.role: An Icon instance after the label, hidden until Trailing Icon is turned on.

fill.token: per flavour, following the label (overridden on the instance)
fill.boundInside: Icon binds foreground/primary; Button overrides it in every flavour and in disabled since 2026-10-18

anatomy._boxNote: measured at size=small; the authored value is the nested Icon's Size variant, not a token on Button

bySize._note: Every cell is a token name except the two suffixed Px, which are measurements of the rendered file. The icon is NOT sized by a token on Button: its size comes from the nested Icon's Size variant, which Button pins (small -> Icon small, medium and large -> Icon medium). icon.renderedSizePx records what that produces.

byFlavourAndState.note: Colour only; identical at every Size and Shape. 'state=disabled' is the Disabled=true axis, which exists only alongside State=default. Border widths are token-bound: stroke/base draws nothing at all — see the stroke/base issue below before implementing a border for it — while stroke/thin and stroke/thick are the visible weights. Focus always draws border/focus at stroke/thick OUTSIDE the bounds, replacing the resting border. Since 2026-10-18 subtle and outline-subtle draw the same transparent ghost scrim as text (interactive/ghost/background/* at 0 / 0.05 / 0.1 / 0 focused / 0 disabled) instead of a solid interactive/neutral/background/* fill; their border and label tokens are unchanged. The icon column records that Button now overrides the nested Icon's fill in every flavour; the token itself could not be read while the icons are hidden.

subcomponents.name: Icon

glyph.resolvesTo: a glyph name in packages/icons/codepoints.json (e.g. 'verified'); verify before use — 9 Figma icons have no glyph

size._note: renderedBoxPx is measured from the file, not a token binding

subcomponents.note: Button uses only Size=small (at size=small) and Size=medium (at size=medium and large), always Framed=false. Icon's own large step never appears inside a Button. Spec the Icon component separately from its own page.

delivery.note: Both families share codepoints, so the Style axis is a font-family swap, not a different glyph. The glyph takes currentColor, which satisfies the metadata's 'the icon follows the label' without a per-flavour icon token.

siblingsOnPage.name: Icon Button
siblingsOnPage.note: A separate public component set that shares the Button page and has its own metadata frame. It is not a subcomponent of Button; Button's usage guidance points to it for icon-only actions. Spec it separately.

tokens.source: tokens/ — names below resolve there; see tokens/manifest.json for collections, modes and the extension graph
tokens.rule: This spec names tokens only. Resolved values live in tokens/ and are deliberately not duplicated here.

palette.note: The only axis that changes Button's colours.

size.note: Every dimension token Button uses resolves identically in all four modes — Button does not respond to density or breakpoint.

typography.note: Same: label/medium and label/large are identical in all four modes.

states.whatChanges: Background, border and label sit on the default tokens of the chosen flavour.

Filled flavours move their own background token one step. Outline flavours hold their border and shift a neutral background underneath instead. Text flavours raise a ghost scrim from fully transparent. The gradient flavours keep their gradient and slide it toward the end colour rather than swapping it (see Gradient transition). Apart from text-gradient, the label colour does not change on any flavour.
The same mechanism as hover carried one step further. The gradient flavours slide the other way, toward the start colour, rather than collapsing to a flat token (see Gradient transition).
A focus ring is drawn outside the bounds, replacing the resting border rather than adding to it. Identical on all nine flavours, and the only state that changes the control's outer footprint.
Background and label swap to the disabled tokens of their family, and the icon follows the label. No flavour keeps its accent colour, so disabled buttons of different flavours look alike.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing. Every state change is colour-only, with no scale, shadow or elevation shift on any flavour, so a transition should read as a tint change rather than movement. The gradient flavours are the one exception to a plain tint: their gradient moves (see Gradient transition).

gradient and text-gradient keep their gradient through every state and move it rather than replace it. On hover the gradient slides until its end colour covers 100% of the fill (the label's own text on text-gradient); on press it slides the other way until its start colour covers 100%. Leaving or releasing slides it back to the resting two-stop gradient. It must never jump from the gradient to a flat colour: a browser cannot interpolate between a gradient and a solid fill, so that swap shows as a flicker. The hover and pressed variants show where each slide ends, not a separate flat fill.
The only change that alters the control's outer footprint, because the ring is drawn outside the bounds. Leave room around a button in a tight row so the ring is not clipped.
The control re-hugs its label whenever the text changes, so a label swapped at runtime shifts the position of everything beside it in a row.

content.description: A verb phrase naming the action. The button hugs whatever length it is given, there is no truncation and no wrapping.

Toggles visibility only. Button does not re-declare Icon's other properties, but the instance stays exposed, so Icon's glyph, Size and Framed are still reachable in the properties panel. See the Icon Metadata frame for what Icon itself offers, and leave its Size alone, Button pairs it to the label.
The same slot mechanics as Leading Icon, placed after the label instead.

content.type: instance swap on the nested Icon
content.description: Any glyph from the icon library. Both slots arrive holding Verified, which suits almost no real action, so set it deliberately whenever a slot is turned on.

do: Use one primary per view or per group. Everything else steps down to outline, subtle or text so the single most important action stays findable.
Write the label as the verb the user is about to perform, Save rather than OK, so the action still reads clearly on its own.
dont: Don't build an icon-only button by hiding this one's label. Icon Button is a separate square component made for that, and it keeps the touch target correct.
Don't mix Shape values inside one button group. A pill beside a rounded button reads as a mistake rather than a deliberate distinction.

accessibility: Focus is drawn as a ring outside the control and is identical on every flavour, so it stays visible whatever the button sits on.
Disabled is a visual state only. Figma cannot carry the reason an action is unavailable, so put that in nearby text in the implementation.
The icon repeats the label rather than adding to it. An action with no visible label belongs in Icon Button, which still needs an accessible name in code.
Every state change is colour-only, so anything signalled by hover or pressed alone will not reach a keyboard or screen reader user.
Write labels as the verb the user is about to carry out, Save rather than OK, so the action is understandable when read out of context.

layoutTheming.description: Always hugs the label and any visible icons, never fixed. Small grows by 16px for each icon shown, medium and large by 20px.
36px at small (control/sm), 40px at medium (control/md), 48px at large (control/lg). Not resizable independently of Size.
12px (space/md) at small and medium, 16px (space/lg) at large.
4px (space/xs) at every size. The fixed height does the real work.
Item spacing is space/none. The visible separation between an icon and the label comes from the Label wrapper's own horizontal padding, 4px (space/xs) at small and 8px (space/sm) at medium and large.
0 (radius/none) for sharp, 4px (radius/element-sm) for rounded, 9999 (radius/pill) for full. All three are token-bound, so match the container rather than overriding on the instance.
1px drawn inside on outline and outline-subtle, none on the other seven at rest. Focus replaces it with a 2px ring drawn outside the bounds.
16px at small, 20px at medium and large. Large reuses Icon's medium step, so Icon's own large (28px) never appears inside a Button.
label/medium (14/20) at small, label/large (16/24) at medium and large, IBM Plex Sans Medium.

Every fill, border and label colour is bound to an interactive/* token for the flavour. Gradient draws from surface/gradient/*, text-gradient from foreground/gradient/*, and focus from border/focus. No variant hardcodes a colour.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored. Every node below deep-links into Figma, so a screenshot can be pulled on demand and is never stale. Colour and geometry are fully specified by the token names in this spec — a screenshot is a sanity check, not the source of truth.
visualReference.caveat: Every one of the 405 variants hides both icon slots, so no screenshot of this component shows an icon inside a Button — which is why the icon-colour blocker below was found by reading bindings, not by looking.

issues.detail: The gradient variants agree with the intended transition (corrected 2026-10-18: hover slides to the end colour, press to the start). gradient hover binds surface/gradient/end and pressed surface/gradient/start; text-gradient hover foreground/gradient/end and pressed foreground/gradient/start. Each variant shows where its slide ends, as the metadata says. Focus also binds the start colour; the metadata gives focus only the ring, so code keeps the resting gradient at focus.

Built 2026-10-18 in <zds-button>, <zds-icon-button>, react-baseui Button and IconButton: the gradient flavours no longer swap to a flat colour. One gradient three times the size of the fill holds the two stops in its middle third (the resting look is unchanged: start at 0%, end at 87%); hover slides its position until the end colour covers 100%, press until the start colour covers 100%, and the position transitions with the other flavours' tints. text-gradient runs the same slide across the label's text and the icons. Web and React were compared in a browser: pixel-identical at rest, hover and pressed.

The old blocker (the nested Icon kept foreground/primary in every flavour) is addressed in the file: every flavour, at rest and disabled, now carries a fills override on both icon instances, which matches the metadata's 'the icon follows the label'. The overridden token could not be read, because the icons are hidden by default and a hidden instance exposes no layers to a read-only extraction. Icon Button, whose glyph is visible, binds it to the flavour's foreground token (see its spec); expect the same here, and confirm by turning an icon on before relying on it.

stroke/base resolves to 0px in every size mode, although its description reads '= 1px, source: scale/0'. It is the border width on the seven non-outline flavours, so those flavours carry a fully bound but zero-width border. Visually this matches the metadata ('none on the other seven at rest'), but a rebuild that trusts the token name or its description will draw a 1px border where Figma draws none.

The scrim flavours (text, text-gradient, subtle, outline-subtle) set a paint-level opacity of 0 / 0.05 / 0.10 on interactive/ghost/background/*. Those tokens already carry the scrim in their own alpha (default and disabled 0%, hover 5%, pressed 10%, in Light and Dark), so Figma applies it twice: the hover scrim renders at about 0.25% and pressed at 1%, practically invisible. Code binds the tokens directly with no paint opacity (the intended 5% / 10%); the Figma paints should drop their opacity to 1.

Seven dimension tokens state a px value in their description that they do not resolve to: control/sm says 40px resolves 36px; control/md says 48px resolves 40px; control/lg says 56px resolves 48px; space/none says 32px resolves 0px; radius/element-sm says 16px resolves 4px; radius/none says 2px resolves 0px; stroke/base says 1px resolves 0px. The resolved values (not the descriptions) match the metadata's Layout & Theming table, so build from the resolved values.

flavour=positive at Disabled=true takes its border from interactive/secondary/border/disabled, while all eight other flavours use their own family's disabled border token. All resolve to line/subtle, so nothing is visibly wrong, but the binding is inconsistent and will read as a mistake in any generated theme map.

Disabled is modelled as a two-option VARIANT axis rather than a Figma boolean property, and State is a documentation-only axis. In code, disabled is a boolean and hover/pressed/focus are interaction states the implementation drives. Only State=default pairs with Disabled=true (405 = 9 x 3 x 3 x 5), so there is deliberately no disabled+hover treatment.

Figma stores VARIANT options in creation order, so Size reads ['medium','large','small'] and Shape reads ['rounded','sharp','full'] through the API. The metadata's order (small/medium/large, sharp/rounded/full) matches the rendered root widths (76 / 90 / 98) and is the order to ship.

The icon glyph is an INSTANCE_SWAP on the nested Icon, not a Button property, and Icon's Size and Framed stay reachable on the exposed instance. Button pins Size (small -> Icon small; medium and large -> Icon medium) and Framed=false. Whether the glyph becomes a Button prop in code is the implementer's call; Size and Framed should not be exposed.

Icon (2046:15010) is local to the file but lives on the 'Icon' page, and the default glyph it holds ('Verified' -> Style=rounded) lives on the 'Assets' page. Neither is remote, but neither is on the Button page, so this spec covers them only as far as Button binds them.

Icon Button (2338:1763) is a second public 405-variant component set sharing the Button page, with its own metadata frame (4732:1074). It is a sibling, not a subcomponent, and has its own spec: specs/icon-button/icon-button.spec.md.

Motion is intentionally not modelled ('Figma stores no timing'), there are no effect styles or shadows anywhere in the component, and no variant hardcodes a colour: the extraction found zero untokenised visual values (gaps) and zero binding drift across the sampled variants.

palette is the only theme axis that changes Button. Every dimension and typography token it binds resolves identically across all four size and typography modes, so Button does not respond to density or breakpoint in Figma.

States & Triggers says 'Outline flavours hold their border and shift a neutral background underneath instead. Text flavours raise a ghost scrim from fully transparent.' Since 2026-10-18 outline-subtle (and subtle) raise the ghost scrim like text; only outline still shifts a neutral background. The metadata's grouping no longer matches the file.

flavour=gradient, state=pressed at Size=small, Shape=sharp takes its border from border/gradient/start; the other eight size/shape variants use interactive/primary/border/pressed. With a stroke/base border this is invisible today, but it is the only place border/gradient/start appears on Button.

flavour=outline, Disabled=true at Size=large, Shape=full draws interactive/ghost/background/disabled at 0 opacity with interactive/ghost/foreground/disabled; the other eight size/shape variants draw interactive/neutral/background/disabled with interactive/neutral/foreground/disabled. Colour is otherwise identical at every Size and Shape.

Resolved 2026-10-18: <zds-button> and react-baseui Button now draw subtle and outline-subtle (and text, text-gradient) on interactive/ghost/background/* directly, and outline's disabled border is interactive/ghost/border/disabled as in the table. Web and React match on all nine flavours at rest, hover and pressed.

Figma now stores the Flavour options in a different creation order (primary, positive, negative, outline, outline-subtle, text, subtle, gradient, text-gradient). The spec keeps the metadata's order, which is unchanged.
